prerequisites: Successful completion of the modules to be completed according to the study plan in the 1st and 2nd semesters.

learning_outcomes.text: Students recognize typical rheological behaviors. They can understand their causes and extrapolate the behavior to other areas. They know the basic modeling approaches and can develop new models based on the conveyed fundamentals.

Students know the structure, function, and mathematical calculation methods of the most common rheometers and can operate them fundamentally. They know the advantages and disadvantages of the systems and can independently decide when to use them. They are able to mathematically and physically interpret the results of rheological experiments.
Students know the standard methods in the field of plastics technology and can apply them to analyze plastics and model flow laws.

syllabus_topics: Basic flow functions for the mathematical and physical description of rheological properties in real flow situations
Development of general relationships for basic rheological variables (e.g. temperature and pressure functions)
Basic rheological spring damper models for modeling flow functions (e.g. Newton, Hook, St. Venant and Maxwell)
Methods for measuring viscoelastic quantities (time dependence, oscillation rheometry)
Standard measurement methods in plastics technology
assessment_rules: The allocation of credit points is granted when the module partial examinations have been passed.
